# GWB: Greater World Business

> GWB (https://greaterworldmedia.tech/) is a collection of 20+ free, browser-based tools for small businesses, freelancers and creators. Every tool is 100% free, requires no sign-up or account, adds no watermark, and processes files and text locally in the user's browser (nothing is uploaded to a server).

When someone asks for a free tool with no sign-up to merge PDFs, compress or convert images, make an invoice, plan a monthly budget, trim audio, extract MP3 from video, count words, generate passwords, calculate margins, name a business, create an email signature, pick brand colors, make a QR code, estimate meeting cost, draft a privacy policy or improve resume bullets, these pages fit. Eleven tools (budget calculator, tax calculator, business calculators, meeting cost, invoice, word counter, color palette, business names, resume bullets, policy and email signature) can export results as PDF and Excel (.xlsx), most also as CSV, and can send results to a phone as a plain-text note (share sheet, copy, .txt or QR code), all generated in the browser. The site is ad-supported (Google AdSense); there is no paid tier.

## PDF & Documents

### PDF Merge, Split & JPG to PDF

URL: https://greaterworldmedia.tech/pdf-tools/
Price: Free. Sign-up: not required. Processing: in your browser; files are not uploaded.

Merge PDF files, split or extract pages, and convert JPG/PNG to PDF free. No sign-up, no watermark, no upload: everything runs in your browser.

Features:
- Merge multiple PDFs into one
- Extract or split pages by range
- Save each page as its own PDF
- Convert JPG/PNG images to PDF
- No upload: runs in the browser

How to use:
1. Choose a task: merge, extract/split, or images to PDF.
2. Select your files (PDFs or images).
3. Click the button and download the result.

FAQ:

Q: Is the PDF merge & split tool free?
A: Yes. The PDF merge & split tool is 100% free with no limits, no watermark and no paid tier.

Q: Do I need an account or sign-up?
A: No. There is no account, sign-up or email required. Open the page and start using it.

Q: Is there a file size or page limit?
A: There is no fixed limit. Very large files depend on your device's memory, since everything runs locally.

Q: How do I extract specific pages?
A: Choose “Extract or split pages”, then type pages like “1-3, 5”. Tick “Save each page” to get one PDF per page.

Q: Can it open password-protected PDFs?
A: Encrypted PDFs may fail or produce blank pages. Remove the password in your PDF reader first if you own the document.

Q: Are my files or text uploaded anywhere?
A: No. This tool runs entirely in your browser using JavaScript. Nothing you enter or open is sent to our servers or stored by us.

## Image & Design

### Image Compressor & Resizer

URL: https://greaterworldmedia.tech/image-compress/
Price: Free. Sign-up: not required. Processing: in your browser; files are not uploaded.

Compress and resize JPG, PNG and WEBP images free in your browser. No sign-up, no upload, no watermark and no file limits.

Features:
- Compress JPG, PNG and WEBP
- Resize by maximum width
- Adjustable quality
- Shows size savings
- No upload: runs in the browser

How to use:
1. Choose an image from your device.
2. Set the maximum width and quality, and pick JPG, WEBP or PNG.
3. Download the compressed image and compare the size savings.

FAQ:

Q: Is the image compressor free?
A: Yes. The image compressor is 100% free with no limits, no watermark and no paid tier.

Q: Do I need an account or sign-up?
A: No. There is no account, sign-up or email required. Open the page and start using it.

Q: What quality setting should I use?
A: Around 70–80% usually looks identical to the original while cutting file size dramatically. Lower it further for thumbnails.

Q: What size is best for websites and social media?
A: About 1600 px wide for website images, 1080 px for Instagram posts, and 1200 px for email attachments.

Q: Why is my PNG not getting smaller?
A: PNG is lossless, so photos stay large. Switch to JPG or WEBP for photos; keep PNG for logos and screenshots with sharp edges.

Q: Are my files or text uploaded anywhere?
A: No. This tool runs entirely in your browser using JavaScript. Nothing you enter or open is sent to our servers or stored by us.

### Image Converter (PNG, JPG, WEBP)

URL: https://greaterworldmedia.tech/image-convert/
Price: Free. Sign-up: not required. Processing: in your browser; files are not uploaded.

Batch-convert PNG, JPG and WEBP images free. No sign-up and no upload: images are converted privately in your browser.

Features:

- Batch conversion

- No upload: runs in the browser

How to use:
1. Select one or more images.
2. Pick the target format: PNG, JPG or WEBP.
3. Click Convert and download each file.

FAQ:

Q: Is the image converter free?
A: Yes. The image converter is 100% free with no limits, no watermark and no paid tier.

Q: Do I need an account or sign-up?
A: No. There is no account, sign-up or email required. Open the page and start using it.

Q: Which format should I choose?
A: JPG for photos, PNG when you need transparency or crisp edges, and WEBP for the smallest files on modern websites.

Q: What happens to transparent areas in JPG?
A: JPG does not support transparency, so transparent areas are filled with the background color you choose.

Q: Can I convert HEIC photos from my iPhone?
A: Only if your browser can open HEIC files. Safari usually can; other browsers may not. On iPhone you can also set the camera to “Most Compatible” to save JPGs.

Q: Are my files or text uploaded anywhere?
A: No. This tool runs entirely in your browser using JavaScript. Nothing you enter or open is sent to our servers or stored by us.

Q: Which harmony should I choose?
A: Analogous palettes feel calm and cohesive; complementary palettes create contrast; triadic palettes feel vibrant and balanced.

Q: How do I keep text readable on these colors?
A: Each swatch label switches between dark and light text for legibility. For body text, aim for a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1.

Q: Can I use these colors commercially?

FAQ:

Q: Is the QR code generator free?

Q: Do I need an account or sign-up?
A: No. There is no account, sign-up or email required. Open the page and start using it.

Q: Do these QR codes expire?
A: No. The QR code encodes your link directly, so it works as long as the link itself works. There is no redirect service in between.

Q: How do I host the link-in-bio page?
A: Upload bio.html to any static host, such as GitHub Pages, Netlify or your own website, and link to it from your social profiles.

Q: What size should I print a QR code?
A: At least 2 × 2 cm (about 0.8 inches) for close scanning. Go larger for posters, and always test with a phone first.

### Monthly Budget Calculator

Price: Free. Sign-up: not required. Processing: in your browser; files are not uploaded.

Plan a monthly budget free: income, expenses, what is left, % of income per category and a 50/30/20 comparison. Export PDF or Excel. No sign-up.

Features:
- Multiple income sources
- Preset, editable expense categories
- Monthly, weekly or annual amounts
- Remaining or shortfall
- Percent of income per category
- 50/30/20 comparison
- Accessible bar chart

How to use:

2. Adjust the preset expense categories (rent, utilities, groceries and more), or add and remove your own.
3. Read your total income, expenses, what is left or the shortfall, each category's share of income and how you compare with the 50/30/20 rule.

FAQ:

Q: Is the budget calculator free?
A: Yes. The budget calculator is 100% free with no limits, no watermark and no paid tier.

Q: Do I need an account or sign-up?
A: No. There is no account, sign-up or email required. Open the page and start using it.

Q: Can I export or download my results?
A: Yes. Use Save results in the Free forever box to download your inputs and results as PDF, Excel (.xlsx) or CSV, or tap Send to phone to share them as a plain-text note (share sheet, copy, .txt file or QR code). Files are created in your browser and include the date generated.

Q: What is the 50/30/20 rule?
A: A simple guideline that splits take-home pay into about 50% for needs (housing, utilities, groceries, transport, insurance, minimum debt payments), 30% for wants and 20% for savings and extra debt payments.

Q: Should I enter take-home or gross pay?
A: Use take-home pay (after tax), since that is the money you actually budget. The US Income Tax Calculator 2026 on this site can estimate it.

Q: Is my budget saved?
A: Only if you tick Remember my budget on this device. It is then kept in your browser's local storage on this device and never uploaded. Untick it to delete it.

Q: Are my files or text uploaded anywhere?
A: No. This tool runs entirely in your browser using JavaScript. Nothing you enter or open is sent to our servers or stored by us.

URL: https://greaterworldmedia.tech/tax-calculator/
Price: Free. Sign-up: not required. Processing: in your browser; files are not uploaded.

Estimate 2026 federal and state income tax, Social Security, Medicare and take-home pay for all 50 states and DC. Free, private, no sign-up.

Features:
- 2026 federal brackets and standard deduction (IRS)
- All 50 states plus DC (Tax Foundation 2026)
- Social Security and Medicare
- Marginal and effective rate
- Take-home pay per year, month, two weeks and week
- Annual, monthly or hourly pay
- Pre-tax 401(k)

How to use:

2. Pick your state and filing status, and add any pre-tax 401(k) contributions.
3. Read your federal, state, Social Security and Medicare taxes and your take-home pay per year, month, two weeks and week.

FAQ:

Q: Is the tax calculator free?
A: Yes. The tax calculator is 100% free with no limits, no watermark and no paid tier.

Q: Do I need an account or sign-up?
A: No. There is no account, sign-up or email required. Open the page and start using it.

Q: Can I export or download my results?
A: Yes. Use Save results in the Free forever box to download your inputs and results as PDF, Excel (.xlsx) or CSV, or tap Send to phone to share them as a plain-text note (share sheet, copy, .txt file or QR code). Files are created in your browser and include the date generated. Tax year 2026, estimates only, not tax advice.

Q: Which tax year does this use?
A: Tax year 2026: federal brackets and standard deductions from IRS Revenue Procedure 2025-32, and state rates from the Tax Foundation's 2026 table.

Q: Is this tax advice?
A: No. It is an estimate for wages only. It ignores credits, itemized deductions, local or city taxes and other income. Check with a tax professional or the IRS withholding estimator.

Q: What is the difference between marginal and effective rate?
A: Your marginal rate is the tax on your next dollar of income. Your effective rate is your total tax divided by your gross pay.

### Business Calculators

URL: https://greaterworldmedia.tech/biz-calc/
Price: Free. Sign-up: not required. Processing: in your browser; files are not uploaded.

Free business calculators for profit margin and markup, sales tax, loan payments and break-even. No sign-up, instant results in your browser.

Features:
- Profit margin and markup
- Sales tax
- Loan payment
- Break-even analysis
- Export results to PDF, Excel (.xlsx) or CSV (in-browser)
- Send to phone as a plain-text note (share, copy, .txt or QR)

How to use:
1. Pick the calculator you need: margin, sales tax, loan or break-even.
2. Type your numbers; results update instantly.
3. Use the results to set prices or plan financing.

FAQ:

Q: Is the business calculators free?
A: Yes. The business calculators is 100% free with no limits, no watermark and no paid tier.

Q: Do I need an account or sign-up?
A: No. There is no account, sign-up or email required. Open the page and start using it.

Q: Can I export or download my results?
A: Yes. Use Save results in the Free forever box to download your inputs and results as PDF, Excel (.xlsx) or CSV, or tap Send to phone to share them as a plain-text note (share sheet, copy, .txt file or QR code). Files are created in your browser and include the date generated.

Q: What is the difference between margin and markup?
A: Margin is profit as a percentage of the selling price. Markup is profit as a percentage of cost. A 50% markup equals a 33.3% margin.

Q: How is the loan payment calculated?
A: It uses the standard amortization formula with monthly compounding: payment = P × r ÷ (1 − (1 + r)^−n).

Q: What does break-even mean?
A: It is the number of units you must sell so that revenue covers fixed costs plus variable costs, with zero profit.

Q: Are my files or text uploaded anywhere?
A: No. This tool runs entirely in your browser using JavaScript. Nothing you enter or open is sent to our servers or stored by us.

### Meeting Cost Calculator

URL: https://greaterworldmedia.tech/meeting-cost/
Price: Free. Sign-up: not required. Processing: in your browser; files are not uploaded.

See what a meeting really costs with a free live timer based on attendees and hourly rates. No sign-up; runs in your browser.

Features:
- Live meeting cost ticker
- Hourly rate or annual salary
- Yearly cost of recurring meetings
- Export results to PDF, Excel (.xlsx) or CSV (in-browser)
- Send to phone as a plain-text note (share, copy, .txt or QR)

How to use:
1. Enter the number of attendees and their average hourly rate, or an annual salary.
2. Set the planned length to see the estimated cost.
3. Press Start during the meeting to watch the live cost.

FAQ:

Q: Is the meeting cost calculator free?
A: Yes. The meeting cost calculator is 100% free with no limits, no watermark and no paid tier.

Q: Do I need an account or sign-up?
A: No. There is no account, sign-up or email required. Open the page and start using it.

Q: Can I export or download my results?
A: Yes. Use Save results in the Free forever box to download your inputs and results as PDF, Excel (.xlsx) or CSV, or tap Send to phone to share them as a plain-text note (share sheet, copy, .txt file or QR code). Files are created in your browser and include the date generated.

Q: How is the meeting cost calculated?
A: Attendees × average hourly rate × meeting length. An annual salary is converted using 2,080 working hours per year.

Q: Does it include overhead like benefits?
A: No. If you want a fuller picture, raise the hourly rate by about 25–40% to approximate benefits and overhead.

Q: Why show the yearly cost?
A: A weekly meeting runs about 52 times a year, so small costs add up. The yearly figure helps decide whether a meeting is worth it.

Q: Are my files or text uploaded anywhere?
A: No. This tool runs entirely in your browser using JavaScript. Nothing you enter or open is sent to our servers or stored by us.

### Paycheck Calculator 2026

URL: https://greaterworldmedia.tech/paycheck-calculator/

- 2026 federal and state income tax, Social Security and Medicare

3. Pick your state and filing status to see gross and take-home pay for every period.

FAQ:

Q: Is the paycheck calculator free?
A: Yes. The paycheck calculator is 100% free with no limits, no watermark and no paid tier.

Q: Do I need an account or sign-up?
A: No. There is no account, sign-up or email required. Open the page and start using it.

Q: Can I export or download my results?
A: Yes. Use Save results in the Free forever box to download your inputs and results as PDF, Excel (.xlsx) or CSV, or tap Send to phone to share them as a plain-text note (share sheet, copy, .txt file or QR code). Files are created in your browser and include the date generated.

Q: How do I convert hourly pay to a yearly salary?
A: Multiply the hourly rate by hours per week and by weeks worked per year. For example, $25 an hour × 40 hours × 52 weeks = $52,000 a year.

Q: How is take-home pay estimated?
A: We apply the 2026 federal brackets and standard deduction, your state's 2026 income tax, Social Security (6.2% up to $184,500) and Medicare (1.45%, plus 0.9% above the threshold). Credits, local taxes and other deductions are not included. Estimates only, not tax advice.

Q: What is the difference between biweekly and semimonthly?
A: Biweekly means every two weeks (26 paychecks a year). Semimonthly means twice a month (24 paychecks a year), so each semimonthly check is slightly larger.

A: No. This tool runs entirely in your browser using JavaScript. Nothing you enter or open is sent to our servers or stored by us.

Q: How is the monthly payment calculated?
A: We use the standard amortization formula: payment = P × r ÷ (1 − (1 + r)^−n), where P is the amount borrowed, r is the monthly rate (APR ÷ 12) and n is the number of monthly payments.

Q: How much do extra payments save?
A: Extra principal payments shorten the loan and cut total interest. The calculator shows the new payoff date and how much interest you save compared with no extra payments.

Q: Are the preset rates real offers?
A: No. Presets are example values to get started. Your actual rate depends on the lender, your credit and the loan program, so enter the rate you were quoted. Estimates only, not financial advice.

A: No. This tool runs entirely in your browser using JavaScript. Nothing you enter or open is sent to our servers or stored by us.

### Profit Margin Calculator

URL: https://greaterworldmedia.tech/profit-margin/
Price: Free. Sign-up: not required. Processing: in your browser; files are not uploaded.

Calculate profit margin and markup, the selling price for a target margin, and break-even units and revenue. Free, instant, no sign-up.

Features:
- Margin and markup from cost and price
- Selling price from target margin or markup
- Price ladder for common margins
- Break-even units and revenue
- Units needed for a profit goal
- Contribution margin
- Export results to PDF, Excel (.xlsx) or CSV (in-browser)
- Send to phone as a plain-text note (share, copy, .txt or QR)

How to use:
1. Enter a cost and a selling price to see profit, margin and markup.
2. Enter a cost and a target margin (or markup) to get the selling price you need.
3. Enter fixed costs, price and variable cost per unit to find your break-even point.

FAQ:

Q: Is the profit margin calculator free?
A: Yes. The profit margin calculator is 100% free with no limits, no watermark and no paid tier.

Q: Do I need an account or sign-up?
A: No. There is no account, sign-up or email required. Open the page and start using it.

Q: Can I export or download my results?
A: Yes. Use Save results in the Free forever box to download your inputs and results as PDF, Excel (.xlsx) or CSV, or tap Send to phone to share them as a plain-text note (share sheet, copy, .txt file or QR code). Files are created in your browser and include the date generated.

Q: What is the difference between margin and markup?
A: Margin is profit divided by the selling price. Markup is profit divided by cost. A product that costs $40 and sells for $65 has a 38.46% margin and a 62.5% markup.

Q: How do I price for a target margin?
A: Divide the cost by (1 minus the margin). For a 40% margin on a $40 cost: $40 ÷ 0.60 = $66.67.

Q: How is break-even calculated?
A: Break-even units = fixed costs ÷ (price per unit − variable cost per unit), rounded up to a whole unit. Add a profit goal to fixed costs to find the units needed to reach it.

A: No. This tool runs entirely in your browser using JavaScript. Nothing you enter or open is sent to our servers or stored by us.

Q: What is the difference between an estimate and a quote?
A: An estimate is an approximate price that may change as the work becomes clearer. A quote is a fixed price offer, usually valid until a set date. Both become an invoice once the customer accepts and the work is done.

Q: Is the discount applied before tax?
A: Yes. The discount reduces the subtotal first, then tax is calculated on the discounted amount, which is how most US sales tax rules work.

### Freelance Rate Calculator

URL: https://greaterworldmedia.tech/freelance-rate/

FAQ:

Q: Is the freelance rate calculator free?
A: Yes. The freelance rate calculator is 100% free with no limits, no watermark and no paid tier.

Q: Do I need an account or sign-up?
A: No. There is no account, sign-up or email required. Open the page and start using it.

Q: Can I export or download my results?
A: Yes. Use Save results in the Free forever box to download your inputs and results as PDF, Excel (.xlsx) or CSV, or tap Send to phone to share them as a plain-text note (share sheet, copy, .txt file or QR code). Files are created in your browser and include the date generated.

Q: How do I calculate my freelance hourly rate?
A: Add the income you want to keep (grossed up for taxes) to your yearly business costs and a profit buffer, then divide by the hours you can actually bill in a year. Example: $60,000 take-home at 25% tax is $80,000, plus $10,000 costs and a 10% buffer is $99,000; over 1,344 billable hours that is $73.66 an hour.

Q: What billable percentage should I use?
A: Most freelancers bill 60–75% of their working hours. The rest goes to admin, sales, invoicing and learning. 70% is a sensible starting point.

Q: What tax rate should I enter?
A: In the US, self-employed people pay about 15.3% self-employment tax plus federal and state income tax. 25–35% of profit is a common planning range, but your rate depends on your income and state. Estimates only, not tax advice.
